scope: Wall real-world outcome consent and account boundary; no whole-system grade change
behavior: Wall events capture owner/session before token work; owned API rechecks identity and a bounded lifetime after awaits. Withdrawal, logout, account change, background, and disposal invalidate pending transport work.
Outcome permission starts closed and is refreshed by lifecycle/consent/auth events, without application polling. A stale consent response cannot grant another session permission.

A durable account-local withdrawal hold is written before network work and remains after offline failure/restart. Only a successful current explicit grant clears it. Storage failure still attempts server withdrawal; memory stays closed.
Settings immediately shows local withdrawal, disables duplicate writes, exposes explicit withdrawal retry, and rejects prior-account read/write results.

4030 takes FOR SHARE on the authoritative consent row inside outcome insertion; existing consent UPDATE/upsert conflicts with that lock. Exact grant timestamp rejects old-grant delayed events after regrant.

The service-only RPC forces the authenticated actor and returns admitted count; absent, stale, withdrawn, unreadable and legacy missing-provenance outcomes are refused. Direct INSERT is guarded as well.
Ordinary Wall product telemetry keeps existing policy. Existing 30-day expiry and account-deletion cascade remain; this migration does not invent historical erasure policy.

limitations: 4030 and this API/client patch are not activated. Parent owns full-chain CI/catalog validation and rollout; Replit origin access was declined and no workaround was used.
Native physical-device background/resume, network abort and storage-failure behavior remain unverified; native Jest is controlled lifecycle evidence, not device proof.

Another device withdrawing while this device stays foreground is enforced by the database admission boundary. This patch does not add a Realtime consent publication; local cached permission refreshes on existing auth/foreground/local consent events.

If device persistence and network withdrawal both fail, the in-memory hold remains until restart but durable restart protection cannot be guaranteed. The UI exposes retry; no successful remote withdrawal is claimed.
No change to outcome canonical-success attribution, exposure denominators, playback summaries, or other systems; those independent audit findings remain open.
Native PostgreSQL tests prove source migration behavior on a minimal schema, not every production trigger interaction. Full-chain CI remains necessary before activation.
